summary: The paper compares five fabricated Ti3C2Tx electrodes: pristine Pure-MXene and Ni-intercalated MXene containing 0.5%, 1%, 10%, or 15 wt% Ni nanoparticles. Ti3C2Tx was produced by HCl/LiF etching of Ti3AlC2, and Ni was incorporated by paste mixing 40 nm Ni powder into the MXene slurry. The headline 10% Ni-MXene delivered 208 F g−1 gravimetric capacitance, 1540 F cm−3 at 10 mV s−1, and 26 Wh kg−1 at 1872 W kg−1; it also retained 83.7% after 10000 cycles. Gravimetric capacitances were reported as 294, 74, 105, 208, and 151 F g−1 for Pure-, 0.5%, 1%, 10%, and 15% Ni-MXene, respectively, but the text does not explicitly associate those values with scan rate or current density. Mass loading, pore parameters, and areal capacitances were not reported.
